headline: {leaderName} signs 'Lawful Cities' order
body: Cities that receive federal funds must verify the immigration status of people using public services. The order takes effect in 30 days. Several mayors say they will sue.

headline: Agents run ID checks at three transit hubs
body: Federal agents checked identification at subway entrances in three cities this morning. The administration called it a pilot. Commuters reported long lines and some arrests.

headline: Judge pauses clinic reporting rule
body: A federal judge temporarily blocked the rule requiring public clinics to report patient status. {leaderName} called the ruling 'activism' and promised an appeal.

headline: {leaderName} unveils plan to clear citizenship backlog
body: The plan adds 2,000 case officers and sets a two-year target for applications older than five years. Republicans in the Senate say the cost is too high.

headline: Language-access rule signed
body: Clinics and agencies that receive federal money must now offer interpreters on request. Advocates say the hard part is making sure people know to ask.

headline: Governors push back on interpreter mandate
body: Eleven governors called the language-access rule an unfunded mandate. Two states say they will not enforce it at state-run clinics.

headline: Fifth Street Clinic visits fall after ID policy
body: Staff at the Fifth Street Clinic say walk-in visits dropped by a third since the new desk policy. 'People are skipping follow-ups,' said one nurse, who asked not to be named.

headline: Library citizenship class finds a new room
body: After attendance fell, Elm Street Library moved its citizenship class to the Grand Avenue center, where organizers say students feel safer signing in.

headline: Grand Avenue center hires bilingual social worker
body: A new federal grant will fund a Mandarin- and Cantonese-speaking social worker at the Grand Avenue Community Center for two years.

headline: Association questions 'cultural plaza' plan
body: The Elm Street Neighborhood Association says the proposed plaza on the Fifth Street lot was 'decided before residents were asked.' A public hearing is set for next month.
